messages:
maria.c: Heads up — customer legal asked for a copy of exported audit events for an upcoming compliance review. We need a quick check: what fields do we include in exports today and who can request them?
aj: Export schema includes timestamp, event_type, actor{id, email}, resource{id, type, tenant_id}, action_details, and signature (when signing enabled).
sasha: signing is optional atm, enabled for some orgs via KMS. But exports currently do not include any viewer_role or disclosure-level metadata.
kevin: that's a problem — customers want to prove who actually saw an event (admin vs member) in their own audit trail. We should surface the role the actor had at event time, and also the visibility of the exported record.
naomi: +1. Suggest adding two fields: "viewer_role" (admin|member|service) and "disclosure_level" (redacted|partial|full). Keep them nullable for backwards compat.
audit-bot: KMS rotation notice: key audit-signing-key-v1 scheduled for rotation 2025-06-12 02:00 UTC. New key audit-signing-key-v2 will be used for v2 signatures.
maria.c: Good note. For schema change we need: 1) minimal backwards compatibility, 2) customer-facing contract/validator, 3) enforcement for scoped tokens so someone with member role can't request full-export for another tenant.
aj: Implementation plan: add optional fields viewer_role and disclosure_level to the event schema; update export service to include viewer_role derived from RBAC service at event time (store snapshot in events). For signed events: use KMS sign v2 format: "sig_v2":"v2:KMS:<base64>" and publish signing_key_id.
sasha: Storing role snapshots means a migration for historical events. We can start by populating for new events and backfill only recent window (90 days). For older exports, mark disclosure_level="unknown" and document.
kevin: Contract validation: produce a small validator script customers can run to verify signatures and required fields. Example event for contract tests: ```{"timestamp":"2025-05-01T15:12:04Z","event_type":"route.update","actor":{"id":"u-123","role":"admin"},"resource":{"id":"r-999","type":"model","tenant_id":"t-abc"},"viewer_role":"admin","disclosure_level":"full","details":{},"sig_v2":"v2:KMS:MEUCIQ...","signing_key_id":"audit-signing-key-v2"}```
naomi: We'll need a docs section that explains verification steps: 1) fetch public verify params from our KMS-verify endpoint, 2) canonicalize event JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace), 3) verify signature scheme v2. I'll draft RFC with examples.
maria.c: RBAC enforcement: exports endpoint must validate requester token scope. Scoped tokens should carry export:read:tenant:<tenant_id> or export:read:org. If token lacks exact tenant scope, deny or return masked events.
aj: Agree. For compatibility add a query param ?mask_sensitive=true default false for internal use. Public exporter should never return full tenant identifiers to a requester lacking tenant export scope. We'll add contract tests for that too.
sasha: For rollout: feature-flag schema_v2, sign new events with key-v2, enable viewer_role population. Can deploy to dedicated exports first, then hosted. Canary at 1% of exports for 48h, run contract tests.
aomi: Who takes ownership of the RFC and validator script? I can write draft docs.
aj: I'll take the PR for service changes and contract test harness. Assigning to @aj.
maria.c: Cool — timeline: RFC by next Tue, PR for schema + RBAC checks in 2 weeks, canary after QA. Naomi, please include sample validator (node/python) in RFC.
aomi: on it. I'll ping @kevin for sample canonicalization edge cases (timestamps, null ordering).
kevin: will add notes. Also need an ops playbook for rotated keys: signed export consumers should accept both v1 and v2 signatures during rotation window.
maria.c: Good call. Add to RFC recovery steps: how to prove export authenticity if key rotated mid-window.
aomi: Drafting now, will post RFC link here when ready.
audit-bot: RFC created: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/1234 (schema + export visibility).
